comments.body:
## Finding: the reduction in the current proof is INCORRECT (verified counterexample)

The NP-hardness theorem is plausibly true, but the reduction in solution.tex does NOT work, in both its original (item due B-a_i+r) and "corrected" (item due N-a_i+r) forms. I rewrote solution.tex to document this honestly.

ERROR: Lemma lem:no claims each window's B item jobs form complete chains (no straddle). FALSE: a chain may straddle a window boundary with separator p_t sitting between two of its jobs, at zero cost in the corrected instance (items are never tardy there). So the window-counting fact (which IS correctly proved) is satisfiable by ANY packing; the 3-Partition structure is never actually used.

VERIFIED COUNTEREXAMPLE: m=2, B=13, a=(4,4,4,4,4,6). This is a valid strongly-bounded NO instance of 3-PARTITION (sum=mB=26; five 4's and one 6 cannot be split into two triples each summing to 13). The corrected scheduling instance (N=28, item due N-a_i+r, separator due t(B+1)) has a feasible T=0 schedule:
  pos 1-12: chains A1,A2,A3; pos13: a_{4,1}; pos14: p_1 (due 14); pos15-17: a_{4,2..4} [A4 STRADDLES the boundary]; pos18-21: A5; pos22-27: A6; pos28: p_2 (due 28).
Every item job sits at position <= 28 with due date >= 23, so all item tardiness is 0; both separators hit their deadlines exactly => T=0. Exhaustive DP confirms the optimum is 0 for this NO instance AND for the YES instance (4,4,4,4,5,5); hence the threshold Y=0 does NOT separate YES from NO. The reduction collapses (a NO 3-Partition instance maps to a YES scheduling instance).

WHY IT IS NOT A QUICK FIX: once the separators meet their deadlines, item jobs are forced onto fixed per-window position-blocks (B positions per window); total item tardiness is then merely an assignment cost over fixed positions, and chain precedence never blocks distributing/splitting a chain across them. Large item slack => splitting is free (collapse to T=0); tight item slack => even valid partitions incur cost that depends on intra-window chain ORDER, not on the partition. I scanned the item staircase offset c0 with separators at t(B+1) over the available small NO/YES instances (B=13, B=20, m=2) and found no choice yielding a clean, scalable YES/NO gap. A correct reduction needs a different gadget in which straddling a boundary is STRICTLY costly (e.g. delaying one chain job forces a later, tightly-due job to be tardy).

PRESERVED / STILL VALID: membership in NP; the block-cost and spreading lemmas; the window-counting consequence of separator deadlines (f(t)=tB, sigma(p_t)=t(B+1)); plus a precise, verified proof that the proposed reduction fails.

STATUS: marking in_progress. I disproved the current reduction and pinned the exact obstruction with a machine-verified counterexample, but I did not supply a complete correct reduction to finish the NP-hardness proof (the remaining task is a straddle-penalizing gadget).
